comparisons.peer_summary: AMD has an approved stock repurchase program authorizing up to $12 billion in repurchases, with $4.7 billion available as of December 28, 2024, which may be suspended or discontinued at any time and could affect cash reserves and stock volatility.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose details of their stock repurchase programs, noting that the authorizations do not obligate the company to purchase any specific amount of stock and that the programs may be suspended or discontinued. However, the scale differs significantly: MU has authorized up to $10 billion with $300 million expended in 2024, while AMD has authorized up to $12 billion with $4.7 billion remaining available for future repurchases as of its fiscal year end.

sentences.text: Our expenditures for these share repurchases were $300 million in 2024, $425 million in 2023, $2.43 billion in 2022, $1.20 billion in 2021, $176 million in 2020, and $2.66 billion in 2019.
Although our Board of Directors has authorized share repurchases of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock, the authorization does not obligate us to repurchase any common stock.
We have an approved stock repurchase program that authorizes repurchases of up to $12 billion of our common stock (Repurchase Program).
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under the Repurchase Program.
The Repurchase Program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Obligations and Capital Return Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks related to its significant debt obligations ($51.0 billion in senior unsecured notes as of Dec 28, 2024) and cyclical industry nature, which pose risks to its financial condition, including potential credit rating downgrades that have already occurred in 2024. Additionally, Intel has ceased stock repurchases and suspended its quarterly dividend in Q4 2024, with additional restrictions under the CHIPS Act agreement creating uncertainty regarding future dividend payments or share repurchases.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC discuss the lack of obligation to execute share repurchases and the uncertainty regarding whether they will enhance shareholder value. A key difference is the current status: MU actively executed $300 million in repurchases in 2024 under its authorization, whereas INTC explicitly states it has ceased stock repurchases and suspended its dividend, highlighting a divergent capital allocation strategy despite similar risk language regarding the non-obligatory nature of such programs.

sentences.text: The amount and frequency of our share repurchases may fluctuate, and we cannot guarantee that we will purchase all of the shares under our share repurchase authorization, or that it will enhance long-term shareholder value.
Our expenditures for these share repurchases were $300 million in 2024, $425 million in 2023, $2.43 billion in 2022, $1.20 billion in 2021, $176 million in 2020, and $2.66 billion in 2019.

In addition, we are not obligated to make repurchases under our stock repurchase program and there can be no assurances as to the amount, timing, and execution of any future share repurchases, or that any repurchases will enhance long-term stockholder value.
